destination.name: Parkes
destination.tagline: A Central West town 20 km from the Dish, the radio telescope that helped bring the Apollo 11 landing to television.
destination.description: Parkes is a Central West town of 9,832 people (2021 census) on the Newell Highway. Parkes Observatory, 20 km north, hosts Murriyang, the 64 m radio telescope known as The Dish, completed in 1961 and added to the Australian National Heritage List in 2020. Its visitors centre has exhibits on the telescope and space science, a 3D theatre and a cafe. Forbes, 33 km south-south-west, has the Plane on a Stick by its main bridge.
whyVisit: Watch the Parkes radio telescope move
Photograph the Plane on a Stick

goodToKnow.title: Phones off at the gate
goodToKnow.detail: Parkes Observatory is a radio-quiet site, so CSIRO asks visitors to turn off mobile, WiFi and Bluetooth when approaching; entry is free, 8:30 am to 4:15 pm daily, with the cafe open 8 am to 3 pm.

goodToKnow.title: Elvis Festival in January
goodToKnow.detail: The Parkes Elvis Festival runs for five days around the second weekend of January with more than 200 events, so expect a busy town then.

goodToKnow.title: Forbes is a separate town
goodToKnow.detail: The Plane on a Stick is in Forbes, 33 km south-south-west on the Newell Highway, so it is a drive rather than a walk from Parkes.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}: summer maximums average about 32C and frequently reach 40C, while winters are cool and partly cloudy.
